technical.clientSecretHandling: Confidential apps send client_id and client_secret to the token endpoint as form parameters or HTTP Basic auth. With PKCE, code_verifier is sent and client_secret becomes optional. Rotating the secret in Settings doesn't break existing user tokens; they move to the new secret on their next refresh.

refreshTokens.notes: All OAuth2 apps were migrated to refresh tokens on April 1, 2026. Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token (rotation); a lost refresh response can be replayed within a 30-minute grace period.

redirectUriRules: Register callback URLs on the app; a manifest allows 1 to 32 unique absolute http or https URLs
The redirect_uri sent at token exchange must match the one used in the authorize request
Exact-match and localhost rules aren't documented

profiles.intent: Read and write issues in any user's workspace

scopes.name: read
scopes.purpose: Default and always present; reads issues, teams and the viewer (the Stage 1 check)

scopes.name: write
scopes.purpose: General write access to the user's account; needed to update issues, not just create them

scopes.name: issues:create
scopes.purpose: Narrower alternative if you only create issues (and their attachments) and never edit them

testModeLimits.text: No test or development tier is documented. A private app (the default) can only be used in the workspace that created it; switching distribution to public lets other workspaces install it.

configGotchas.text: Turn on Public (distribution: public) or other workspaces can't install the app; private is the default.
Store the new refresh token after every refresh; the old one is replaced.
App names can't contain "Linear" or start with http:// or https://.

stage1.summary: Self-serve for a workspace admin: create an OAuth2 application in Settings > Administration > API, add a callback URL, and run one code flow.

stage2.summary: No review, verification or fee is documented for a public OAuth app acting as the user: setting distribution to public makes it installable by other workspaces. Each customer workspace on a paid plan can turn on Third-Party App Approvals, so their admin may have to approve you first.

time.startsWhen: when a member of a workspace with Third-Party App Approvals turned on requests approval

stage1DoneWhen.text: POST https://api.linear.app/graphql with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and the query { viewer { id name email } } returns the authorizing user's id, and your token response included a refresh_token and expires_in of about 86399.

blockedBy.how: On any paid plan, a workspace admin (owner on Enterprise) can turn on Third-Party App Approvals; members then can't install your app until it's approved, and a denial is shown to them with its reason.
Leaving the app private (the default) means only your own workspace can authorize it. Creating the app also needs admin rights in the workspace that owns it.
Per-user rate limits apply (5,000 requests and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour for OAuth apps); raising them is case by case through support.

profiles.bottomLine: A first token takes one sitting if you're a workspace admin. No review stands between a public app and other workspaces; the real risks are tenant admins who require app approval and rotating refresh tokens that break under concurrent refreshes.
topRisks: Forgetting to set the app to Public keeps every other workspace out
Rotating refresh tokens: a stale or double refresh returns invalid_grant and forces the user to reconnect
Customer workspaces with Third-Party App Approvals on block members until an admin approves

steps.title: Pick the workspace that will own the app
instructions: Use a dedicated workspace for the OAuth app: every admin in that workspace gets access to it.
You need admin permissions in that workspace to open the API settings page.

steps.title: Create the OAuth2 application
instructions: Go to Settings > Administration > API and create a new OAuth application (direct form: https://linear.app/settings/api/applications/new).
Fill in the application name (2 to 80 characters, no "Linear", no http(s):// prefix), developer name, and a homepage or docs URL. An icon and description are optional.
Add your callback URL(s) under the callback/redirect URLs field (up to 32, absolute http or https).
Leave client credentials off; this intent uses the authorization code flow.
Optional: build the form as a manifest and pass it as URL parameters to pre-fill the page.

steps.title: Turn on Public so other workspaces can install
instructions: Switch the app's distribution from private (default) to public.
Without it, only your own workspace can authorize the app.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
instructions: Copy the client ID and client secret from the app's page.
Keep the secret on your server or in a secret manager. Public clients should use PKCE, where the secret is optional.
If it leaks, use Rotate secret next to the client secret in Settings > API.

steps.title: Send a user through the authorize URL
instructions: Open https://linear.app/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_URI&response_type=code&scope=read,write&state=RANDOM
Scopes are comma-separated. Use read,issues:create instead if you never edit issues.
Leave actor unset (defaults to user) so issues are created as the person who authorized.
For PKCE add code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. Add prompt=consent to let a user connect another workspace.
Approve, then check that the state returned with code matches what you sent.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
instructions: POST to https://api.linear.app/oauth/token with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
Send grant_type=authorization_code, code, the same redirect_uri, client_id, and client_secret (or code_verifier for PKCE). Basic auth also works for the client credentials.
Store access_token, refresh_token, expires_in and scope. Apps created before December 1, 2023 get scope back as an array.

steps.title: Check the token works
instructions: POST https://api.linear.app/graphql with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and { viewer { id name email } }.
Expect the user's id back. To test writes, query teams for a teamId and run issueCreate with title and teamId.

steps.title: Wire up token refresh
instructions: Access tokens last 24 hours. Before expiry, POST grant_type=refresh_token and refresh_token to the token endpoint (PKCE tokens need only client_id).
Each refresh returns a new refresh token: save it atomically and allow one refresh per connection at a time.
If a refresh response is lost to a network error, replay the same request within 30 minutes to recover the new token.

steps.title: Handle customer workspaces that require app approval
instructions: If a customer workspace has Third-Party App Approvals turned on, a member who tries to install your app sees a request screen and can add a reason.
Their admin (owner on Enterprise) gets an email and in-app notification and approves or denies on the workspace Applications page; the member is told the outcome.
Give customers a short description of what your app does with their issues to help the request through. No timeline is documented.

requirements.label: Admin seat in the owning workspace
requirements.detail: The API settings page that holds OAuth applications is admin-only; every admin of that workspace can see the app.
requirements.howToPrepare: Create or choose a dedicated workspace where you are admin.

requirements.label: App name, developer name and homepage URL
requirements.detail: Name and developer name 2 to 80 characters; the app name can't include "Linear" or an http(s):// prefix. Homepage or docs URL required; description (up to 1,000 characters) and icon (256x256 recommended) optional.
requirements.howToPrepare: Pick a name without "Linear" in it and have a public homepage ready.

requirements.label: Callback URL
requirements.detail: At least one absolute http or https redirect URL (up to 32).
requirements.howToPrepare: Register the exact URL your server will send as redirect_uri.

limits.value: 5,000 requests per hour per user (or app user)
limits.whenHit: GraphQL returns HTTP 400 with a RATELIMITED error code; X-RateLimit-Requests-* headers show the reset. Support can raise limits case by case.

limits.value: 2,000,000 complexity points per hour per user
limits.whenHit: Same RATELIMITED error; track X-RateLimit-Complexity-* and per-query X-Complexity headers.
The query is rejected outright; split it or paginate.

limits.what: Who can install a new app
limits.value: Only the owning workspace (distribution defaults to private)
limits.whenHit: Other workspaces can't authorize until you set the app to public.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your workspace can't authorize the app
blockers.cause: The app is still private, the default distribution
blockers.fix: Turn on Public (distribution: public) in the app's settings

blockers.cause: A stale refresh token after rotation, often two workers refreshing at once, or the user revoked the app
blockers.fix: Persist each new refresh token atomically and serialize refreshes; replay within the 30-minute grace window; otherwise ask the user to reconnect

blockers.cause: Per-user hourly request or complexity budget exhausted
blockers.fix: Back off until the reset header; reduce query complexity; ask support for a temporary increase

blockers.symptom: Member sees a request-approval screen instead of the consent screen
blockers.cause: The workspace has Third-Party App Approvals turned on
blockers.fix: The member requests approval and a workspace admin approves it on the Applications page

blockers.symptom: Creating issues works but updates fail
blockers.cause: Only issues:create was requested, which covers creating issues and attachments
blockers.fix: Request write and have users re-authorize

nuances.text: Since April 1, 2026 all OAuth2 apps use refresh tokens with 24-hour access tokens. Ignore older guides that mention a Refresh Tokens toggle or 10-year tokens.
Refresh tokens rotate on every refresh, with a 30-minute grace window to replay a lost response.

actor=user (default) makes changes as the authorizing person, which fits this intent. actor=app installs the app into the workspace as its own app user, needs admin permissions to install, can't be combined with the admin scope, and is aimed at agents and service accounts.
A public actor=user app is installable by other workspaces; the integration directory is required only for agents.

The integration directory is a separate listing that accepts useful integrations from formal companies (not scripts or hobby apps) and asks for icons and showcase images. It isn't needed for an actor=user public app.
The page may appear as Settings > Administration > API or Settings > API > OAuth applications. Same page.
Scopes are comma-separated in the authorize URL. Apps created before December 1, 2023 receive scope as an array in the token response.
OAuth tokens use Authorization: Bearer TOKEN; personal API keys go in the Authorization header without Bearer.
Revoke on disconnect with POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/revoke and a token form field (optional token_type_hint).
OAuth rate limits are counted per user, not per app; workspace-level apps using actor authorization get higher limits based on paid seats.

notFound.why: No review, security assessment, business or domain verification, fee or legal-entity requirement found. Recorded as not_mentioned, not as "not required".
